players.product: Aurora sodium fast-reactor SMR powerhouses for data-center power (1.2 GW Ohio campus for Meta; Aurora-INL 2028 startup)

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2025 results (pre-revenue), per CFO: loss from operations of $139.3 million (driven by payroll, general business expenses and professional fees), including non-cash stock-based compensation of $41.8 million; loss before income taxes of $110.2 million after $29.1 million of interest and dividend income. Cash used in operating activities was $82.2 million, or $69.2 million adjusted for about $13 million of prepaid capital project expense - within the 2025 guidance of $65 million to $80 million.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 loss from operations $139.3 million; operating cash use $82.2 million ($69.2 million adjusted) vs. $65 million to $80 million guidance

quarterly_data.signal: Balance sheet and financing: Oklo ended 2025 with cash and marketable securities of $1.4 billion and in the first month of 2026 raised an additional $1.182 billion net of fees, completing its $1.5 billion ATM program. CFO says Oklo is 'very well capitalized for 2026 and beyond'; asset-level/project financing is not yet executed but is part of the long-term capitalization strategy, with discussions under way with EDF (which 'used to be the loan program office').
quarterly_data.figure: $1.4 billion cash and marketable securities (year-end 2025); $1.182 billion raised in the first month of 2026 completing $1.5 billion ATM

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 guidance introduced on this call: cash used in operating activities raised from the 2025 range to $80 million to $100 million (to expand headcount across the three business units), and cash used in investing activities between $350 million and $450 million, spanning powerhouse deployment at Idaho National Laboratory (called 'an important piece of that spend') and preliminary work for the Meta powerhouses in Ohio, the Tennessee recycling project, isotope projects including Groves, and scoping capex for HALEU, plutonium and transuranic fuel projects. No project-by-project breakdown given; CFO expects 2027 capex to 'continue to see CapEx that will be at those levels'.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 operating cash use $80 million to $100 million; investing cash use between $350 million and $450 million

quarterly_data.signal: Aurora-INL (first Aurora powerhouse, DOE Reactor Pilot Program): OTA executed and Nuclear Safety Design Agreement approved; site characterization complete, site preparation including blasting under way. Responses received for the majority of long-lead component RFPs, supplier down-selection under way, and 'all major equipment now has vendors under contract' - including the Siemens Energy power conversion system, reactor module component agreements and all major refueling equipment. Management targets a 2028 time line (described as aggressive), with the full plant reaching nuclear heat production in 2028; cost of the first asset to be shared later this year. CEO: pretty much every part outside of the fuel can come from outside the conventional nuclear supply chain.

Customer pipeline: CFO says Meta is the anchor customer and conversations continue with Meta and other announced and unannounced customers - data centers (including behind-the-meter on-campus customers), the U.S. military (predominantly in Alaska) and industrial customers. CEO says since the Meta deal, inbound has shifted toward 'meaningful binding offtakes' with prepayment-like structures, and 'we don't see a shortage of need or appetite'. On why Meta chose Oklo (alongside TerraPower as the fast-reactor picks): fast-reactor technical maturity and sodium cost benefits, multiple fuel pathways, and an existing ROFR and land access in Ohio.

Fuel ('one of the most significant rate limiters for new nuclear deployment'): A3F fuel fabrication facility at INL received DOE approval of the NSDA and PDSA (the first facility approved under DOE's Advanced Nuclear Fuel Line Pilot Program) and began initial construction so fuel fabrication does not gate Aurora-INL. Tennessee Advanced Fuel Center (first recycling step): geotechnical surveys done, NRC pre-application engagement completed, rolling NRC readiness review initiated, selected for DOE recycling R&D funding; agreement signed with TVA to explore fuel recycling. Potential deconversion joint venture with Centrus at Centrus' Pike County, Ohio site, co-located with its enrichment operations and adjacent to Oklo's planned 1.2 gigawatt campus. Completed a fast-spectrum plutonium criticality experiment with Los Alamos National Laboratory; DOE plutonium awards still under review.

Isotopes: Groves radioisotope test reactor in Texas - site development and structure completed in 5 months, reactor tank installed, fuel procured, execution target of criticality by July 4 (CEO 'pretty confident' of hitting or beating it). The Idaho Radiochemistry Laboratory obtained its NRC materials license (delayed in the fall by the government shutdown) and is expected to make first revenue this year.
quarterly_data.figure: Groves criticality target July 4; structure completed in 5 months

quarterly_data.signal: Licensing strategy: DOE authorization for first-of-a-kind DOE-site assets (Aurora-INL, A3F, Groves) and the NRC pathway for commercial assets (Aurora Ohio, Tennessee Advanced Fuel Center, Idaho Radiochemistry Laboratory). Oklo expects the NRC to soon issue its approach for converting a DOE-authorized facility to an NRC license, and for Ohio 'we still expect a Part 52 combined license' while NRC regulatory rewrites under the executive orders could change the application vehicle and reduce costs and time lines.

connects_to.relationship: Aurora powerhouse nuclear power supply from Oklo's 1.2 GW Ohio campus

contracts.signal: Early 2026 prepayment agreement with Meta in support of a 1.2 gigawatt Aurora campus in Pike County, Ohio: phased deployment with an initial phase of 150 megawatts targeted around 2030, supported by a prepayment-for-power structure; Oklo expects to use the prepayment funds to support fuel procurement and owns approximately 206 acres in Pike County. CEO calls it 'a binding commitment to provide power' that sets the stage for pre-procurement of the longest-lead items (fuel), with a PPA expected to come together 'over the next year or so'.
